part: walking-surface slope from midstance for the 50 UMich 2021 treadmill recordings (evidence for D-UM21-T02-2)
requested_by: José: use midstance to get the true ground slope.
summary: The motion shared by AB01 i5 and AB01 i10 was walked on a 10-degree incline. Midstance foot path gives 10.09 deg (IQR 9.98-10.20), heel-toe pitch minus the level offset gives 11.00 deg (10.68-11.25), and plate force tilt gives 9.76 deg (9.60-9.90). AB01 i10 is correctly labelled. AB01 i5 is the mislabelled copy, as D-UM21-T02-2 already assumed. Every method flags AB01 i5, and no other recording disagrees with its label on the marker methods.
changed_files: contributor_tools/review_um21_t02_clock.py (D-UM21-T02-2 slope figure replaces the hip-trace figure; slope added to chips, why, option B and check)
not_changed: backlog.json/html, AGENTS.md, converted_datasets/, source folders, the audit script and its tests, D-UM21-T02-1 (its decision.json is byte-identical to the previous build).

method.frames: Markers are in the lab frame (README: global coordinates, m). Up = lab +z: the pelvis is above the heel in 50/50 recordings. Forward = the median horizontal heel->toe direction. The stance foot moves backward along it in 97.1-100 % of strides. Plates are in the local plate frame (README).
method.midstance: Strides 0.7-2.0 s. Foot-flat frames fall between 10 % and 50 % of the stride, where |v_heel - v_toe| <= 0.05 m/s (heel and toe carried together by the belt), with at least 3 per stride. The fixed 25-35 % window is also reported. In AB04, AB09 and others the foot still rotates there (0.1-0.2 m/s), which biased it in blind run 1.

estimates.foot_pitch: José's method: heel->toe pitch atan2(dz, d.forward) at the foot-flat frames, minus the same participant's and leg's level (i0) median.
estimates.belt_path: Pitch of the flat foot's path (mean heel/toe velocity) at the same frames, with belt speed >= 0.4 m/s. No offset is needed.
estimates.plate_force: Tilt of the stride-mean total GRF (L+R plates) from the plate normal. The plate +y sign comes from braking-before-propulsion order. Valid only when the plates carry the full body weight, which is reported per recording.

method.tolerance: Fixed in code before AB01 i5/i10 values were seen. A --blind run withheld both, and the final run reproduced the blind tolerances exactly, with the same probe sha. Per method, over the 38 non-level recordings other than AB01 i5/i10: tol = max(1, ceil_0.5(|median residual| + 4 x 1.4826 x MAD)). Result: belt_path 2.5 deg (robust SD 0.52), foot_pitch 5.5 deg (robust SD 1.28), plate_force 1.0 deg (robust SD 0.08). Only plate_force has tol < 2.5 under the rule. The AB01 answer does not depend on that, because all three methods put the motion at 9.8-11.0 deg, nearest label 10.
method.development_log: Blind run 1 used the fixed window only. The foot-flat gate and the plate body-weight check were added after blind runs 1-2, using the other 48 recordings only. The tolerance rule was not changed.

results.verdict: 10-degree incline. AB01 i10's label is correct; AB01 i5's label (5 deg) is wrong by about 5 deg. AB01 has no recording walked at 5-degree incline in this source.
results.plate_d5_question: The earlier verifier saw a 2.25-deg plate tilt on a d5 recording. Only AB03 d5 (-1.79 deg) and AB10 d5 (-2.16 deg) look like that, and there the plates carry only 0.93 and 0.94 body weights per stride. The other 8 d5 recordings give -4.92 to -5.02 deg with 0.99-1.01 body weights. In AB03 and AB10 the plates carry 0.91-0.98 body weights, least on declines. The tilt shrinks with the missing weight, which fits support off the plates (for example a handrail; not verified). The midstance foot path agrees with the label in all of them (AB03 d5 -5.20, AB10 d5 -5.21 deg). The README 5 deg holds. In the other 38 recordings (8 participants, AB01 i5/i10 excluded), the plate tilt is within -0.25 to +0.09 deg of the label.

side_findings_not_acted_on: Forceplate force is in N, not the README's N/kg: the stride-mean |GRF| equals body mass x 9.81 (0.99-1.01 body weights in full-weight recordings).
AB03 and AB10 plates carry 3-9 % less than body weight, most on declines. Any UM21 kinetics release should check this before using their plate forces.

checks_run.probe_blind: nice 19, ionice idle, single-thread env, RLIMIT_AS soft 768 MiB, one recording at a time; peak RSS 192.9 MiB
checks_run.probe_final: same; peak RSS 192.7 MiB, 8.5 s; --blind-report tolerances equal
checks_run.render: Playwright Chrome at 1100 and 390 px: scrollWidth = viewport, details closed, 3/3 images load, recommendation not visible
checks_run.tests: OPENBLAS/OMP/MKL=1 MPLBACKEND=Agg nice 19 ionice -c3 pytest -q tests/test_audit_um21_tread_pilot*.py tests/test_backlog_workflow.py: 114 passed. build_backlog_page.py --check: Backlog valid; HTML current (88 tasks). No tests cover the probe itself; its evidence is the reproducible blind/final pair.

not_checked: Why AB01 i5 holds a copy, or whether an original AB01 5-degree recording exists elsewhere (authors not asked).
Why the AB03/AB10 plates carry less than body weight (handrail or harness use is a hypothesis only).
Per-participant marker placement changes between sessions; the level offset assumes the same placement across one participant's treadmill trials.
remaining: Independent review. The coordinator re-copies D-UM21-T02-2 from decisions_for_backlog into backlog.json. The option letters and their order are unchanged; option B's consequence, why and check text changed.
next_action: Second agent: re-run the probe with --blind into a new path and confirm the same tolerances. Then re-run it unblinded with --blind-report and confirm the AB01 values and flags. Inspect review_sheets/D-UM21-T02-2 at both widths.
